classification.difficultyReason: Independently set up the three-sided fencing constraint, form the area quadratic, locate its maximum and recover both dimensions using the taught river-field method.

content.prompt:
A farmer has 100 m of fencing to form a rectangular paddock with a river on one side (that does not require fencing), as shown.
What will be the dimensions of the paddock to achieve its maximum area?

spec.description: River above a rectangular paddock; its upper side is the unfenced riverbank. The other three sides are red fencing. The right side is labelled x m. Decorative water strokes are simplified.
spec.mathematics: Two equal perpendicular fenced sides have length x; the third fenced side lies parallel to the river. No numerical dimensions are supplied in the figure.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent student reference diagram; contains no solved dimensions.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the breadth and $y$ the length, in metres. Only three sides require fencing.
$$\begin{align*}2x+y &= 100\\y &= 100-2x\\A &= xy\\A &= x(100-2x)\\A &= 2x(50-x)\end{align*}$$
The area parabola is concave down and has zeros at $x=0$ and $x=50$. Its maximum occurs halfway between these values.
$$\begin{align*}x &= \frac{0+50}{2}\\x &= 25\\y &= 100-2(25)\\y &= 50\end{align*}$$
The paddock should have breadth 25 m and length 50 m.
